hooks.text: Astronauts saved a melting space station with a giant umbrella.
Did a giant umbrella save America's first space station?
America's high-tech space station was saved by a homemade sunshade.

title: The Billion-Dollar Space Umbrella
description: When Skylab's heat shield failed during launch, NASA engineers had to invent a cosmic sunshade to save the station from melting.

beats.text: Astronauts saved a melting space station with a giant umbrella.
beats.visual: fly-around photograph of Skylab showing the deployed parasol sunshade, 1973

beats.text: Many think our first station was a custom-built fortress.
beats.visual: cutaway diagram showing the S-IVB stage repurposed as a space station

beats.text: It was actually a repurposed rocket stage.
beats.visual: photograph of the Skylab orbital workshop on the ground before launch

beats.text: Launch forces in 1973 ripped away its vital heat shield.
beats.visual: Skylab 2 fly-around damage photo showing the missing micrometeoroid shield, 1973

beats.text: Internal temperatures spiked to a dangerous 130 degrees.
High heat threatened to release toxic gases from the insulation.
beats.visual: photograph of the interior of the massive Skylab orbital workshop, 1973

beats.text: Engineers rushed to build a makeshift fabric sunshade.
beats.visual: photograph of NASA engineer Jack Kinzler with a model of the sunshade

beats.text: The crew shoved this parasol through a tiny porthole.
beats.visual: photograph of the Skylab 2 crew inside the workshop, 1973

beats.text: Then a risky spacewalk sent the men cartwheeling into space.
beats.visual: illustration of astronauts cartwheeling in space during the solar panel repair

beats.text: It was a billion-dollar station saved by a giant umbrella.
beats.visual: fly-around photograph of Skylab with the parasol sunshade deployed, 1973

better_than_last: Applied the myth_vs_fact structure by opening on the misconception of Skylab as a finished fortress versus its actual state as a damaged rocket stage.
